sources.heading: Average order value
sources.text: AOV = recorded payment revenue / number of delivered orders with at least one payment row. AOV excludes delivered orders with missing payments and reports their count. Multiple payment installments/sequences do not increase the order denominator. A zero denominator yields NULL. State means customer state, not seller state.

sources.heading: Successful orders and revenue
sources.text:
A successful order has `order_status = 'delivered'`. Revenue means the sum of recorded `payment_value_cents` for these orders. Aggregate all payment sequences per order first. The result includes any freight contained in the recorded payments. It is a gross payment-based proxy, not profit, net revenue, cash-flow timing or accounting revenue: refund, cost and settlement data are unavailable. Canceled, unavailable and all other non-delivered statuses are excluded.

Orders without payment rows have unknown payment value, not zero. Always report delivered orders, delivered orders with payments, and missing-payment coverage separately. Zero-valued recorded payments are legitimate observed values for this calculation. A sum over no eligible payments is NULL, not invented zero revenue.

Currency is BRL; storage and reference totals use integer cents. Divide by 100 for presentation. Do not sum payments after a raw join to items or reviews.

sources.heading: Payments, installments and item value
sources.text:
Each order can have multiple payment sequences, payment types and installments. A payment row is not another order, and installment count is not a multiplier for `payment_value_cents`. Aggregate the recorded payment values per order once. Zero-value recorded payments differ from absent payment records.

Item prices and item freight are separate measures. Do not assume item prices equal recorded payments or infer refunds, discounts, settlement times or margin from their difference. The source does not contain a refund ledger, marketing spend or product cost data.

  FROM orders

    o.order_status,
    p.total_payment_cents
  FROM orders o
  LEFT JOIN order_payments p ON o.order_id = p.order_id
),
monthly_agg AS (
  SELECT
    pm.purchase_month,
    mb.first_month,
    mb.last_month,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_status = 'delivered' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_orders,

    SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.total_payment_cents IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_missing_payment,
    SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.total_payment_cents IS NOT NULL THEN o.total_payment_cents ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents

    CASE WHEN purchase_month = first_month OR purchase_month = last_month THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS boundary_month

  delivered_orders,

sources.text: Cancellation rate = orders with status exactly `canceled` / all orders in the selected purchase cohort. `unavailable` is a distinct status, not automatically a cancellation. sources.heading: Successful orders and revenue
sources.text:
A successful order has `order_status = 'delivered'`. Revenue means the sum of recorded `payment_value_cents` for these orders. Aggregate all payment sequences per order first. The result includes any freight contained in the recorded payments. It is a gross payment-based proxy, not profit, net revenue, cash-flow timing or accounting revenue: refund, cost and settlement data are unavailable. Canceled, unavailable and all other non-delivered statuses are excluded.

Orders without payment rows have unknown payment value, not zero. Always report delivered orders, delivered orders with payments, and missing-payment coverage separately. Zero-valued recorded payments are legitimate observed values for this calculation. A sum over no eligible payments is NULL, not invented zero revenue.

Currency is BRL; storage and reference totals use integer cents. Divide by 100 for presentation. Do not sum payments after a raw join to items or reviews.

sources.heading: Average order value
sources.text: AOV = recorded payment revenue / number of delivered orders with at least one payment row. AOV excludes delivered orders with missing payments and reports their count. Multiple payment installments/sequences do not increase the order denominator. A zero denominator yields NULL. State means customer state, not seller state.

sources.heading: Category and seller sales; freight
sources.text:
Item sales = sum of `price_cents` on delivered orders. Freight = separate sum of `freight_value_cents`. These measures exclude non-delivered orders and do not use payment value. An item is a source line item; repeated products on an order are still separate item rows.

Category/seller rankings explicitly say **item sales**, not payment revenue. Payment-based revenue cannot be uniquely assigned across categories/sellers without an allocation policy. The baseline intentionally does not invent one. Missing categories form an explicit NULL/Unknown group; untranslated categories keep the Portuguese label. Group on the raw category key, not the display label, to avoid label collisions.

sources.heading: Payments, installments and item value
sources.text:
Each order can have multiple payment sequences, payment types and installments. A payment row is not another order, and installment count is not a multiplier for `payment_value_cents`. Aggregate the recorded payment values per order once. Zero-value recorded payments differ from absent payment records.

Item prices and item freight are separate measures. Do not assume item prices equal recorded payments or infer refunds, discounts, settlement times or margin from their difference. The source does not contain a refund ledger, marketing spend or product cost data.

sources.heading: Seller and region screening
sources.text:
Seller sales/rating screen: require at least 20 reviewed delivered orders, retain sellers whose mean selected order score is below the platform's order-weighted mean across reviewed delivered orders, and rank by delivered item sales (top 20). This is a candidate review list; high sales means relative ranking, not a statistical threshold.

Seller late-delivery screen: require at least 30 eligible delivered orders and a late rate above the platform eligible-order late rate; rank by rate, then sample size, then seller ID (top 20). This is an above-average descriptive screen, not an anomaly test or proof of seller fault. Thresholds are configurable named SQL parameters.

Category delivery ranking requires at least 30 eligible order/category pairs. Regional delivery reports show all customer states with order counts, eligible deliveries, late counts/rates and mean delivery days; no arbitrary high-volume or poor-performance cutoff is implied. Carrier, route and geography may confound seller comparisons.

sources.heading: Delivery eligibility, lateness and duration
sources.text:
Eligible delivery = status `delivered`, non-null delivered and estimated timestamps, and delivered timestamp >= purchase timestamp. Excluded delivered orders are counted. This is a purchase-to-customer metric and does not require a carrier timestamp.

Late means `order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date` using the full timestamp. Equality is on time. Arrival later on the estimated calendar date counts late under this strict rule; this is deliberate and must be disclosed. A calendar-day sensitivity count is also reported, but does not replace the strict definition. NULL dates are unknown, never on time.

Late rate = late eligible orders / all eligible delivery orders. Delivery days = elapsed purchase-to-customer seconds / 86,400, not rounded calendar days or business days. A category contributes at most once per order to category delivery analysis, even if an order has several items in that category. A multi-category order can appear in several category groups, so group order counts are not additive.

sources.heading: Successful orders and revenue
sources.text:
A successful order has `order_status = 'delivered'`. Revenue means the sum of recorded `payment_value_cents` for these orders. Aggregate all payment sequences per order first. The result includes any freight contained in the recorded payments. It is a gross payment-based proxy, not profit, net revenue, cash-flow timing or accounting revenue: refund, cost and settlement data are unavailable. Canceled, unavailable and all other non-delivered statuses are excluded.

Orders without payment rows have unknown payment value, not zero. Always report delivered orders, delivered orders with payments, and missing-payment coverage separately. Zero-valued recorded payments are legitimate observed values for this calculation. A sum over no eligible payments is NULL, not invented zero revenue.

Currency is BRL; storage and reference totals use integer cents. Divide by 100 for presentation. Do not sum payments after a raw join to items or reviews.

sources.heading: Order lifecycle
sources.text:
The supplied orders file contains these observed status labels: `created`, `approved`, `invoiced`, `processing`, `shipped`, `delivered`, `canceled`, and `unavailable`. They describe the snapshot's recorded status. The file does not provide a complete sequence of status-change events, so do not infer exact transition paths or time spent in each state.

Purchase, approval, carrier handoff, customer delivery and estimated delivery are separate timestamps. Some are missing or inconsistent. Do not fill missing timestamps with purchase dates or infer successful delivery from an estimate. The project's successful-order definition is exactly status `delivered`; delivery-duration metrics additionally need eligible observed timestamps.

Scores range from 1 to 5; poor means 1 or 2. First retain reviews with creation >= order purchase and answer timestamp >= review creation. Multi-seller orders contribute their order score to each associated seller; comparisons are therefore not independent seller-level experiments.

sources.heading: Delivery eligibility, lateness and duration
sources.text:
Eligible delivery = status `delivered`, non-null delivered and estimated timestamps, and delivered timestamp >= purchase timestamp. Excluded delivered orders are counted. This is a purchase-to-customer metric and does not require a carrier timestamp.

Late means `order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date` using the full timestamp. Equality is on time. Arrival later on the estimated calendar date counts late under this strict rule; this is deliberate and must be disclosed. A calendar-day sensitivity count is also reported, but does not replace the strict definition. NULL dates are unknown, never on time.

Late rate = late eligible orders / all eligible delivery orders. Delivery days = elapsed purchase-to-customer seconds / 86,400, not rounded calendar days or business days. A category contributes at most once per order to category delivery analysis, even if an order has several items in that category. A multi-category order can appear in several category groups, so group order counts are not additive.

sources.heading: Seller and region screening
sources.text:
Seller sales/rating screen: require at least 20 reviewed delivered orders, retain sellers whose mean selected order score is below the platform's order-weighted mean across reviewed delivered orders, and rank by delivered item sales (top 20). This is a candidate review list; high sales means relative ranking, not a statistical threshold.

Seller late-delivery screen: require at least 30 eligible delivered orders and a late rate above the platform eligible-order late rate; rank by rate, then sample size, then seller ID (top 20). This is an above-average descriptive screen, not an anomaly test or proof of seller fault. Thresholds are configurable named SQL parameters.

Category delivery ranking requires at least 30 eligible order/category pairs. Regional delivery reports show all customer states with order counts, eligible deliveries, late counts/rates and mean delivery days; no arbitrary high-volume or poor-performance cutoff is implied. Carrier, route and geography may confound seller comparisons.

sources.heading: Category and seller sales; freight
sources.text:
Item sales = sum of `price_cents` on delivered orders. Freight = separate sum of `freight_value_cents`. These measures exclude non-delivered orders and do not use payment value. An item is a source line item; repeated products on an order are still separate item rows.

Category/seller rankings explicitly say **item sales**, not payment revenue. Payment-based revenue cannot be uniquely assigned across categories/sellers without an allocation policy. The baseline intentionally does not invent one. Missing categories form an explicit NULL/Unknown group; untranslated categories keep the Portuguese label. Group on the raw category key, not the display label, to avoid label collisions.

Seller sales/rating screen: require at least 20 reviewed delivered orders, retain sellers whose mean selected order score is below the platform's order-weighted mean across reviewed delivered orders, and rank by delivered item sales (top 20). This is a candidate review list; high sales means relative ranking, not a statistical threshold.

Seller late-delivery screen: require at least 30 eligible delivered orders and a late rate above the platform eligible-order late rate; rank by rate, then sample size, then seller ID (top 20). This is an above-average descriptive screen, not an anomaly test or proof of seller fault. Thresholds are configurable named SQL parameters.

Category delivery ranking requires at least 30 eligible order/category pairs. Regional delivery reports show all customer states with order counts, eligible deliveries, late counts/rates and mean delivery days; no arbitrary high-volume or poor-performance cutoff is implied. Carrier, route and geography may confound seller comparisons.

sources.heading: Review score and poor reviews
sources.text:
Scores range from 1 to 5; poor means 1 or 2. First retain reviews with creation >= order purchase and answer timestamp >= review creation. Among those, select the latest answer timestamp per order; break ties by latest creation timestamp, then lexicographically largest review ID. This is deterministic and avoids weighting orders by their number of reviews. It is a snapshot policy, not evidence that the selected review was a revision of another one.

Missing eligible reviews are excluded from score averages and reported separately. For late-versus-on-time comparison, restrict to eligible deliveries and show review coverage, mean score, poor-review count and rate by group. Differences describe association only. No statistical test, significance claim or causal attribution is performed in Phase 2.

Seller ratings are **order-level review scores associated with the seller**, not direct seller ratings. Count each order/seller pair once, even for repeated items. Multi-seller orders contribute their order score to each associated seller; comparisons are therefore not independent seller-level experiments.

sources.heading: Category and seller sales; freight
sources.text:
Item sales = sum of `price_cents` on delivered orders. Freight = separate sum of `freight_value_cents`. These measures exclude non-delivered orders and do not use payment value. An item is a source line item; repeated products on an order are still separate item rows.

Category/seller rankings explicitly say **item sales**, not payment revenue. Payment-based revenue cannot be uniquely assigned across categories/sellers without an allocation policy. The baseline intentionally does not invent one. Missing categories form an explicit NULL/Unknown group; untranslated categories keep the Portuguese label. Group on the raw category key, not the display label, to avoid label collisions.

WITH
-- Filter to delivered orders
DeliveredOrders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
),

-- Get latest eligible review per order (per definitions)
LatestOrderReviews AS (
    SELECT r.order_id, r.review_score
    FROM reviews r
    JOIN DeliveredOrders d ON r.order_id = d.order_id
    WHERE r.review_creation_date >= d.order_purchase_timestamp
      AND r.review_answer_timestamp >= r.review_creation_date
      AND r.review_answer_timestamp = (
          SELECT MAX(r2.review_answer_timestamp)
          FROM reviews r2
          WHERE r2.order_id = r.order_id
      )
      AND r.review_creation_date = (
          SELECT MAX(r3.review_creation_date)
          FROM reviews r3
          WHERE r3.order_id = r.order_id
            AND r3.review_answer_timestamp = r.review_answer_timestamp
      )
      AND r.review_id = (
          SELECT MAX(r4.review_id)
          FROM reviews r4
          WHERE r4.order_id = r.order_id
            AND r4.review_answer_timestamp = r.review_answer_timestamp
            AND r4.review_creation_date = r.review_creation_date
      )
),

-- Join items with delivered and reviewed orders
SellerOrderItems AS (
    SELECT oi.seller_id, oi.order_id, oi.price_cents
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN DeliveredOrders d ON oi.order_id = d.order_id
),

-- Aggregate reviews per order and join sellers
SellerOrderReviews AS (
    SELECT soi.seller_id, soi.order_id,
           LOR.review_score
    FROM SellerOrderItems soi
    JOIN LatestOrderReviews LOR ON soi.order_id = LOR.order_id
    GROUP BY soi.seller_id, soi.order_id
),

-- Count delivered orders and reviewed orders per seller
SellerOrderCounts AS (
    SELECT seller_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS delivered_orders_count
    FROM SellerOrderItems
    GROUP BY seller_id
),

SellerReviewedCounts AS (
    SELECT seller_id,
           COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS reviewed_orders_count,
           AVG(CAST(review_score AS REAL)) AS mean_review_score_per_seller
    FROM SellerOrderReviews
    GROUP BY seller_id
),

-- Calculate platform-wide mean review score (order-level weight)
PlatformReview AS (
    SELECT AVG(CAST(review_score AS REAL)) AS platform_mean_review_score
    FROM LatestOrderReviews
),

-- Calculate item sales per seller for delivered orders
SellerSales AS (
    SELECT seller_id,
           SUM(price_cents) AS item_sales_cents
    FROM SellerOrderItems
    GROUP BY seller_id
),

-- Combine all seller metrics
SellerMetrics AS (
    SELECT soc.seller_id,
           soc.delivered_orders_count AS delivered_orders,
           SRC.reviewed_orders_count AS reviewed_orders,
           SS.item_sales_cents,
           ROUND(SRC.mean_review_score_per_seller, 6) AS mean_review_score
    FROM SellerOrderCounts soc
    LEFT JOIN SellerReviewedCounts SRC ON soc.seller_id = SRC.seller_id
    LEFT JOIN SellerSales SS ON soc.seller_id = SS.seller_id
),

FilteredSellers AS (
    SELECT sm.*, pr.platform_mean_review_score
    FROM SellerMetrics sm, PlatformReview pr
    WHERE sm.reviewed_orders >= 20
      AND sm.mean_review_score < pr.platform_mean_review_score
)

SELECT seller_id, delivered_orders, reviewed_orders, item_sales_cents, mean_review_score, ROUND(platform_mean_review_score, 6) AS platform_mean_review_score
FROM FilteredSellers
ORDER BY item_sales_cents DESC, seller_id ASC
LIMIT 20
;

WITH eligible_orders_sellers AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        o.order_id,
        o.order_delivered_customer_date,
        o.order_estimated_delivery_date
    FROM
        order_items oi
    JOIN
        orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE
        o.order_status = 'delivered'
        AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
        AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
        AND o.order_delivered_customer_date >= o.order_purchase_timestamp
    GROUP BY
        oi.seller_id, o.order_id
),

seller_delivery_stats AS (
    SELECT
        seller_id,
        COUNT(order_id) AS eligible_orders,
        SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders
    FROM
        eligible_orders_sellers
    GROUP BY
        seller_id
),

platform_stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS platform_eligible_orders,
        SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS platform_late_orders
    FROM (
        SELECT
            order_id,
            order_delivered_customer_date,
            order_estimated_delivery_date
        FROM
            orders
        WHERE
            order_status = 'delivered'
            AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
            AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
            AND order_delivered_customer_date >= order_purchase_timestamp
        GROUP BY
            order_id
    )
),

platform_late_rate AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN platform_eligible_orders = 0 THEN NULL
            ELSE CAST(platform_late_orders AS FLOAT) / platform_eligible_orders * 100.0
        END AS platform_late_pct
    FROM
        platform_stats
)

SELECT
    s.seller_id,
    s.eligible_orders,
    s.late_orders,
    ROUND(CAST(s.late_orders AS FLOAT) / s.eligible_orders * 100.0, 6) AS late_pct,
    ROUND(plr.platform_late_pct, 6) AS platform_late_pct
FROM
    seller_delivery_stats s,
    platform_late_rate plr
WHERE
    s.eligible_orders >= 30
    AND CAST(s.late_orders AS FLOAT) / s.eligible_orders * 100.0 > plr.platform_late_pct

sources.heading: Delivery eligibility, lateness and duration
sources.text:
Eligible delivery = status `delivered`, non-null delivered and estimated timestamps, and delivered timestamp >= purchase timestamp. Excluded delivered orders are counted. This is a purchase-to-customer metric and does not require a carrier timestamp.

Late means `order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date` using the full timestamp. Equality is on time. Arrival later on the estimated calendar date counts late under this strict rule; this is deliberate and must be disclosed. A calendar-day sensitivity count is also reported, but does not replace the strict definition. NULL dates are unknown, never on time.

Late rate = late eligible orders / all eligible delivery orders. Delivery days = elapsed purchase-to-customer seconds / 86,400, not rounded calendar days or business days. A category contributes at most once per order to category delivery analysis, even if an order has several items in that category. A multi-category order can appear in several category groups, so group order counts are not additive.

WITH EligibleOrders AS (
    SELECT
        oi.seller_id,
        o.order_id,
        o.order_delivered_customer_date,
        o.order_estimated_delivery_date,
        o.order_purchase_timestamp
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
      AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date >= o.order_purchase_timestamp
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id, o.order_id
),
LateStats AS (
    SELECT
        seller_id,
        COUNT(order_id) AS eligible_orders,
        SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders
    FROM EligibleOrders
    GROUP BY seller_id
    HAVING eligible_orders >= 30
),
PlatformLate AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS platform_eligible_orders,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS platform_late_orders
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
      AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date >= o.order_purchase_timestamp
),
PlatformLateRate AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
          WHEN platform_eligible_orders = 0 THEN NULL
          ELSE 100.0 * platform_late_orders / platform_eligible_orders
        END AS platform_late_pct
    FROM PlatformLate
),
SellerLateRates AS (
    SELECT
        ls.seller_id,
        ls.eligible_orders,
        ls.late_orders,
        CASE
          WHEN ls.eligible_orders = 0 THEN NULL
          ELSE 100.0 * ls.late_orders / ls.eligible_orders
        END AS late_pct
    FROM LateStats ls
),
SellerWithPlatform AS (
    SELECT
        slr.seller_id,
        slr.eligible_orders,
        slr.late_orders,
        ROUND(slr.late_pct, 6) AS late_pct,
        ROUND(plr.platform_late_pct, 6) AS platform_late_pct
    FROM SellerLateRates slr CROSS JOIN PlatformLateRate plr
    WHERE slr.late_pct > plr.platform_late_pct
)
SELECT
    seller_id,
    eligible_orders,
    late_orders,
    late_pct,
    platform_late_pct
FROM SellerWithPlatform
ORDER BY late_pct DESC, seller_id ASC
LIMIT 20;

sources.heading: Delivery eligibility, lateness and duration
sources.text:
Eligible delivery = status `delivered`, non-null delivered and estimated timestamps, and delivered timestamp >= purchase timestamp. Excluded delivered orders are counted. This is a purchase-to-customer metric and does not require a carrier timestamp.

Late means `order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date` using the full timestamp. Equality is on time. Arrival later on the estimated calendar date counts late under this strict rule; this is deliberate and must be disclosed. A calendar-day sensitivity count is also reported, but does not replace the strict definition. NULL dates are unknown, never on time.

Late rate = late eligible orders / all eligible delivery orders. Delivery days = elapsed purchase-to-customer seconds / 86,400, not rounded calendar days or business days. A category contributes at most once per order to category delivery analysis, even if an order has several items in that category. A multi-category order can appear in several category groups, so group order counts are not additive.

sources.heading: Successful orders and revenue
sources.text:
A successful order has `order_status = 'delivered'`. Revenue means the sum of recorded `payment_value_cents` for these orders. Aggregate all payment sequences per order first. The result includes any freight contained in the recorded payments. It is a gross payment-based proxy, not profit, net revenue, cash-flow timing or accounting revenue: refund, cost and settlement data are unavailable. Canceled, unavailable and all other non-delivered statuses are excluded.

Orders without payment rows have unknown payment value, not zero. Always report delivered orders, delivered orders with payments, and missing-payment coverage separately. Zero-valued recorded payments are legitimate observed values for this calculation. A sum over no eligible payments is NULL, not invented zero revenue.

Currency is BRL; storage and reference totals use integer cents. Divide by 100 for presentation. Do not sum payments after a raw join to items or reviews.

    o.order_id,
    o.order_status,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp,

    CASE

        AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
        AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
        AND o.order_delivered_customer_date >= o.order_purchase_timestamp THEN 1
      ELSE 0

        AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL
        AND o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1
      ELSE 0

        AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
        AND o.order_delivered_customer_date >= o.order_purchase_timestamp
      THEN (julianday(o.order_delivered_customer_date) - julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp))
      ELSE NULL
    END AS delivery_days
  FROM orders o
  JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
)

  customer_state,
  COUNT(order_id) AS total_orders,
  SUM(eligible_delivery) AS eligible_orders,
  SUM(late_delivery) AS late_orders,
  CASE WHEN SUM(eligible_delivery) = 0 THEN NULL

  CASE WHEN SUM(eligible_delivery) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE ROUND(AVG(CAST(delivery_days AS FLOAT)), 6)
  END AS mean_delivery_days
FROM orders_with_eligibility
GROUP BY customer_state
